breaking.headline: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after 4-hour halt; 2,500+ flights canceled Saturday
breaking.fact: The FAA ordered a rare nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon after a telecommunications failure hit air-traffic-control centers, then lifted it at 8:15 p.m. ET; more than 6,600 flights were canceled Friday and 8,600 delayed, with 2,500+ more canceled Saturday as airlines work through the backlog — the longest nationwide stop since 9/11.

breaking.headline: Fed: AI is now Wall Street's top financial-stability worry
breaking.fact: The Fed's Financial Stability Report, released Friday, found 87% of market contacts cite AI as a salient risk — up from 50% in May — pointing to stretched valuations, cyber risks and complex AI financing; debt tied to advanced computing hit $680 billion by October, five times all of 2023.

breaking.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet Thursday in Shenzhen on nuclear arms
breaking.fact: The White House confirmed Friday that Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen — the first-ever trilateral of the three leaders — to open talks on nuclear arms control nine months after New START expired; officials say no agreement is expected, and the war in Iran is also on the agenda.

breaking.headline: Bitcoin slides below $67,000 as crypto selloff deepens
breaking.fact: Bitcoin fell 6.15% to about $66,950 on Friday as crypto joined the risk-off slide, with Ether down 6% and Solana down 7.7%; the token has given back much of its autumn rally as the Nasdaq's slide and a strong dollar pressured risk assets.

weekInBrief.headline: Nvidia's brutal week: down 12.7% as the CEO search drags on
weekInBrief.body: Nvidia fell 12.7% on the week to $162.85 as the post-Huang slide deepened and the board's CEO search — reportedly including an approach to Arm chief Rene Haas — dragged on; the first post-Huang earnings report lands Tuesday Nov 17.

weekInBrief.headline: UK economy grows 0.7% in Q3, fastest since early 2024
weekInBrief.body: Britain's economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, up from 0.5% in Q2 and the fastest quarterly pace since early 2024, the ONS said Thursday; services rose 0.9%, led by computer programming and AI-related activity, while annual growth picked up to 1.9%.

weekInBrief.headline: China's factory-gate prices jump 5.7%, fastest in over four years
weekInBrief.body: China's producer price index rose 5.7% year on year in October, the fastest since June 2022 and above the 5.3% forecast, the National Bureau of Statistics said Monday; higher energy costs drove the surge while consumer inflation cooled to 0.7%, widening the gap between factory costs and household demand.

weekInBrief.headline: Treasury yields jump as a December Fed hike stays fully priced
weekInBrief.body: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed from 4.86% to 5.15% over the week after October wholesale inflation ran hot at 6.5% year on year, keeping a December Fed rate hike fully priced.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: The U.S. and Iran traded fire in the strait on Friday, the largest threat yet to the pause in fighting, hours after Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it seized the tanker Ocean Koi in the Gulf of Oman and CENTCOM said U.S. forces disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers trying to enter Iranian ports; CENTCOM commander Adm. Bradley Cooper said U.S. forces “remain committed to full enforcement of the blockade.” CENTCOM also said it shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones launched against Bahrain, after the Guard claimed it had destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar there. Early Saturday, Iranian state media claimed three tankers — one a supertanker — caught fire after striking mines in the strait, a claim that gave no vessel names or flags and could not be independently verified. Iran also announced a new “Persian Gulf Strait Authority,” saying ships must email Tehran their origin, cargo and destination before transiting. On oil, Kpler's tracking still shows Iranian crude loadings at zero since late August — the first zero month since tracking began in 2013 — while Reuters, citing UANI tracking and SynMax satellite analysis, reports at least 4.1 million barrels of Iranian LPG have slipped past the blockade on eight tankers since mid-July; non-Iranian crude keeps moving, at about 7.3 million barrels a day through the strait in the week to October 28.

space.headline: Starship's Ship 42 aims for a first-ever catch this afternoon
space.body: Ship 42 is healthy in orbit after Friday's 4:47 p.m. CT liftoff from Starbase, having deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and SpaceX plans the first-ever catch of an upper stage at the tower around 3:19 p.m. CT today after 14 orbits; the double-catch bid already failed at the first hurdle — one engine failed to relight on the boostback burn, the Super Heavy catch was aborted, and Booster 22 was detonated above the Gulf.

space.headline: Rocket Lab's Electron hits 100 launches — fastest commercial rocket ever
space.body: Rocket Lab's Electron flew its 100th mission overnight, “The Mountain God Rises,” launching from New Zealand at 6:30 p.m. local time and deploying the YAMATSUMI-II radar-imaging satellite to a 575 km orbit for Japan's iQPS; reaching 100 launches in under a decade — since its 2017 debut — is a record for a commercially developed rocket, and iQPS has booked seven more Electron flights through 2030.

space.headline: New South African dinosaur was a heavyweight even as a youngster
space.body: Meet Nyana rooiwalensis, a newly identified dinosaur from South Africa that lived more than 200 million years ago and weighed about 400 kilograms (880 pounds) despite still being a youngster; identified from a near-complete skull and other bones, the two-legged sauropodomorph is an early relative of giants like Brachiosaurus, and its Late Triassic age sheds light on how the group diversified.

space.headline: Hamster hibernation study offers clues to Alzheimer's
space.body: Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven found that hibernation triggers changes in hamster brain cells that partly resemble those seen in Alzheimer's disease, with gene-expression shifts across the hibernation cycle echoing the build-up of amyloid plaques; the findings, published in Science Advances, suggest some early Alzheimer's changes may also occur as a natural adaptive response, opening new ways to study the disease.

apod.title: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3
apod.credit: Apollo 12 / Alan Bean — stereo image by Kevin Frank (NASA)
apod.explanation: Put on your red/blue glasses and gaze across the western Ocean of Storms on the Moon: this 3D anaglyph shows Apollo 12 astronaut Pete Conrad visiting the Surveyor 3 spacecraft in November 1969. Surveyor 3 had landed on the inside slope of a small crater about 2 1/2 years earlier, in April 1967, and Apollo 12's Lunar Module Intrepid touched down less than 200 meters away. The stereo image was carefully created from two separate pictures captured on the lunar surface, depicting the scene from slightly different viewpoints, approximating the separation between human eyes.
